vision: Pillai College of Engineering (PCE) will admit, educate and train in technology, a diverse population of students who are academically prepared to benefit from the Institute's infrastructure and faculty experience, to become responsible professionals. It will further attract, develop and retain dedicated, excellent teachers, scholars, scientists and professionals from diverse backgrounds whose work gives them visibility beyond the classroom.
mission: To develop professional engineers with respect for the environment and make them responsible citizens, both from a local and global perspective. This objective is fulfilled through quality education, practical training, research, entrepreneurship and interaction with industries and social organisations.

metrics.title: Curricular planning and implementation
metrics.description: The institution ensures effective curriculum delivery through a well planned and documented process. Explain academic planning, adherence to academic calendar, lesson plans, course files, and teaching methods (e.g. Project-Based Learning, e-learning platforms) used to ensure delivery.
metrics.narrative_draft:
Pillai College of Engineering ensures effective curricular planning and implementation by strictly adhering to the curriculum prescribed by the University of Mumbai. The institution maintains a diligent approach to academic delivery, characterized by the systematic preparation and review of lesson plans. These lesson plans are designed with a specific focus on Bloom's Taxonomy, targeting cognitive levels such as Information, Understanding, Application, and Synthesis to ensure comprehensive learning outcomes. The academic calendar is prepared in advance to guide the semester schedule, and all lesson plans undergo rigorous review by Heads of Departments (HODs) to ensure alignment with institutional standards and university guidelines.

To maintain transparency and accountability, teachers are required to maintain detailed course files. These files document critical academic data, including lecture details, student attendance records, and internal assessment marks, serving as a comprehensive record of teaching and learning activities. A significant institutional initiative is the institutionalization of Project-Based Learning (PBL) from the first year of the program onwards. This approach integrates practical application and collaborative learning into the core curriculum, moving beyond theoretical instruction to foster real-world problem-solving skills.

The delivery of the curriculum is further supported by a robust Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) system that aligns with University of Mumbai guidelines while incorporating specific institutional reforms. The CIE framework includes two Internal Assessment tests (IA1 and IA2) per semester, with questions meticulously mapped to Bloom's Taxonomy levels to assess varying degrees of cognitive engagement. To ensure the quality and consistency of assessment, subject-wise question banks containing at least 150 questions are prepared by faculty and moderated by the HOD. Additionally, the institution introduces a Prelim exam in an open-book format for selected courses, specifically designed to promote application-level learning rather than rote memorization. Laboratory work, mini-projects, and PBL presentations are evaluated using rubric-based methods to provide objective and standardized feedback. Furthermore, the institution supports student success through targeted interventions, such as Study Camps held before prelims for students who score below 40% in IA1, ensuring that no student is left behind in the curricular delivery process.

metrics.title: Institution integrates cross-cutting issues into the curriculum
metrics.description: Institution integrates cross-cutting issues relevant to Professional Ethics, Gender, Human Values, Environment and Sustainability into the Curriculum. Describe courses, workshops, active clubs (like Nature Club), and programs addressing ethics, environment, and gender equity.
metrics.narrative_draft: PillaiCollege of Engineering demonstrates a robust integration of cross-cutting issues into its curriculum, ensuring that professional ethics, human values, and sustainability are not merely theoretical concepts but core components of student learning. The institution has embedded mandatory courses such as 'Business Communication & Ethics,' 'Cybersecurity,' and 'Intellectual Property' (IPR) rights into the academic framework. These courses are designed to instill a strong sense of professional responsibility, ethical conduct, and legal awareness among engineering students, directly addressing the NAAC criteria for professional ethics and human values. Beyond the classroom, the institution actively promotes environmental sustainability and social responsibility through its Nature Club. The club organizes annual cleanliness drives, including a specific project focused on the cleaning of the Gadhi River, as well as tree plantation drives and carbon-neutral campus awareness campaigns. These initiatives provide students with practical experience in environmental stewardship and community engagement. Furthermore, the institution extends its focus on cross-cutting issues through extension activities conducted by the NSS unit, Nature Club, and various student chapters. In the 2023-24 academic year, these groups engaged in 166 extension activities in the neighborhood community, aiming to sensitize students to social issues and foster a sense of civic duty. The institution also supports research and innovation in sustainable technologies, having funded four projects in 2019 focused on AI/ML, IoT, and Renewable Energy. Additionally, workshops and seminars on Intellectual Property Rights and industry-academia innovative practices are regularly conducted, reinforcing the link between ethical academic practices and professional application. This holistic approach ensures that graduates are not only technically proficient but also ethically grounded, environmentally conscious, and socially responsible professionals.

metrics.narrative_draft: Pillai College of Engineering, Panvel, actively promotes the holistic development of its students by offering value-added courses that impart essential transferable and life skills. A significant initiative in this regard is the 'Nirbhaya' Five-Day Intensive Self-Defense & Personal Safety Training Workshop, organized by the Women Development Cell (WDC) in collaboration with the Navi Mumbai Police Commissionerate, specifically the Nirbhaya Pathak Squad. This program was conducted from 11th December 2023 to 15th December 2023 at the Ground Floor Conclave & Gymkhana. The workshop was designed to empower female engineering students and lady staff members with practical skills for personal safety and self-preservation. A total of 320 female students from first, second, and third-year degree programs successfully completed the five-day physical training. The curriculum was comprehensive, covering situational awareness protocols, particularly for public transport commutes, street self-defense maneuvers, and legal protections for women. Additionally, the training included hands-on orientation to emergency response procedures, such as the use of the Police Dial 112 SOS mobile emergency application. The sessions were led by Lady Police Inspector Sunita More and her team, who demonstrated practical martial arts maneuvers and emergency cyber-helpline tools. This initiative not only enhances the physical safety of the students but also equips them with critical life skills that are transferable to various professional and personal contexts. By integrating such practical, safety-oriented training into the academic calendar, the institution demonstrates its commitment to fostering a secure and empowering environment for its students, thereby contributing to their overall well-being and readiness for the challenges of the modern world.

metrics.title: Student diversity (Slow vs. Advanced Learners)
metrics.description: The institution assesses the learning levels of the students, after admission and organises special programs for advanced learners and slow learners. Explain the identification process, mentoring schemes, remedial classes, coaching for competitive exams (GATE, GRE), and research support.
metrics.narrative_draft: PCE implements a structured framework to assess and support student diversity, specifically distinguishing between slow and advanced learners to ensure holistic academic development. The identification process begins immediately after admission, where the institution conducts diagnostic tests and utilizes continuous internal assessments to evaluate the learning levels of all students. This data-driven approach allows for the precise categorization of students based on their academic performance. Slow learners are specifically identified based on their performance in the first internal tests. To address the needs of this group, the institution organizes scheduled remedial classes, specialized study camps, and bilingual tutorial sessions. These interventions are designed to bridge learning gaps and provide targeted support to help these students achieve parity with their peers. Conversely, advanced learners are encouraged to engage in high-level academic and professional activities. The institution facilitates their participation in national-level events such as the Smart India Hackathon, promotes the publication of research papers, and provides specific guidance classes for competitive examinations including GATE, GRE, and CAT. Furthermore, the Training and Placement Cell conducts GATE, GRE, CAT, and civil services guidance sessions, along with career counselling workshops, which benefit a significant portion of the student body, with an average of 4.26% of students directly benefiting from these competitive exam guidance and career counselling initiatives. This dual-track approach ensures that while slow learners receive the necessary remedial support to strengthen their foundational knowledge, advanced learners are provided with the resources and opportunities to excel in research and competitive examinations, thereby catering to the diverse learning needs of the entire student population.

metrics.title: Student-centric methods
metrics.description: Student centric methods, such as experiential learning, participative learning and problem solving methodologies are used for enhancing learning experiences. Elaborate on project-based learning, maker spaces (Maker Studio), industrial visits, virtual labs, and student chapters.
metrics.narrative_draft:
PCE has institutionalized student-centric pedagogical methods, with a primary focus on Project-Based Learning (PBL) that is integrated into the curriculum from the first year of study. This approach ensures that students engage in experiential and participative learning by completing projects that often cross multiple subject boundaries, thereby enhancing interdisciplinary problem-solving skills. The mission of developing responsible professional engineers is explicitly operationalized through PBL, the Maker Studio, community extension, and industry linkages, ensuring that theoretical knowledge is consistently applied to practical scenarios.

To support these learning methodologies, the college has established an advanced Maker Studio equipped with state-of-the-art facilities for rapid prototyping. This space includes 3D printers, laser cutters, PCB milling machines, and CNC machines, allowing students to transform conceptual designs into tangible prototypes. Complementing the Maker Studio is an on-campus Component Library, which provides students with access to electronic sensors, microcontrollers, and actuators. This resource is available for both academic assignments and innovative projects, fostering a culture of hands-on experimentation and maker culture.

The implementation and quality assurance of these student-centric methods are overseen by the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC), established in 2017. The IQAC played a pioneering role in introducing project-based learning and establishing the Component Library. To ensure the effectiveness of these methods, the IQAC conducts annual Academic and Administrative Audits (AAA) to review teaching-learning processes. Furthermore, the Academic Monitoring System (AMS) dynamically tracks attendance, daily lecture entries, and syllabus coverage across all academic programs, providing data-driven insights into student engagement and learning outcomes. Governance structures, including the Academic Council and department committees, regularly review these initiatives to align them with the institution's five-year perspective plans and quality policies, which are displayed in all departments and reviewed annually.

metrics.title: Ratio of students to mentor for academic and stress related issues
metrics.description: Number of mentors allocated and mentor-mentee ratio.
metrics.narrative_draft:
PCE has established a dedicated mentor-mentee scheme designed to provide comprehensive academic and personal support to students. Under this structured framework, a small group of students, approximately 15 to 20 in number, is allotted to a single faculty mentor. This allocation ensures a manageable mentor-mentee ratio, facilitating personalized attention and effective guidance. The mentoring process is systematic and regular, with mentors conducting fortnightly meetings to discuss critical aspects of student life, including academic progress, personal grievances, and career aspirations. These regular interactions help in early identification of stress-related issues and academic challenges, allowing for timely intervention and support.

To ensure accountability and continuous monitoring, the institution maintains detailed mentoring registers. These registers track key indicators such as attendance at mentoring sessions, the psychological well-being of the mentees, and their academic performance. This data-driven approach allows the institution to assess the effectiveness of the mentoring program and make necessary adjustments to improve student outcomes. Furthermore, PCE recognizes the importance of professional psychological support in addressing stress-related issues. In addition to faculty mentors, professional counselors are available on campus to provide confidential psychological counseling. This multi-layered support system ensures that students have access to both academic guidance from faculty and specialized mental health support from trained professionals.

The institution also leverages its broader ecosystem for student development. The PCE Alumni Association, which has 3,850 registered members, organizes mentorship programs as part of its regular activities, including alumni meets and guest lectures. This integration of alumni mentorship complements the faculty-led mentoring scheme, providing students with diverse perspectives and industry insights. Additionally, the Pillai Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (PCIE) offers mentoring services, particularly for students involved in incubation and startup activities. With 14 startups incubated and 3 funded, the PCIE provides a platform for practical mentoring in entrepreneurship. The Drone Lab also contributes to student training, having trained 120 students in drone design and DGCA-aligned training. Collectively, these initiatives create a robust support network that addresses both academic and stress-related issues, ensuring holistic student development.

metrics.narrative_draft:
The institution, Mahatma Education Society (MES), places significant emphasis on the academic upgradation of its faculty, specifically targeting the attainment of doctoral degrees to enhance research capabilities and pedagogical quality. In alignment with NAAC Metric 2.4.2, which tracks the average percentage of full-time teachers with Ph.D. degrees over the last five years, the institution has established a robust framework to support faculty in pursuing higher qualifications. A key initiative in this regard is the MES Faculty Higher Qualification Upgradation Policy, which provides structured support for faculty members undertaking doctoral research. 

Recent records indicate active institutional support for faculty pursuing Ph.D. degrees. For instance, a memorandum dated 10th August 2023 (Ref No: MES/HR/EDU-LEAVE/2023/452) documents the sanction of a six-month paid sabbatical study leave for Prof. Archana Dongre, Associate Professor in the Department of Information Technology. This leave, granted from 1st September 2023 to 28th February 2024, was specifically to enable her to finalize experimental benchmarking and submit her Ph.D. thesis titled 'Optimized Machine Learning Pipelines for Healthcare Telemetry' to the University of Mumbai at Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute (VJTI). The institution provided comprehensive welfare measures, including a monthly doctoral research fellowship allowance, reimbursement of thesis submission and defense fees, and temporary adjustment of teaching workloads to guest faculty to ensure academic continuity. 

While the specific year-wise percentage data for the last five years is not explicitly tabulated in the provided excerpts, the existence of such detailed sanction orders and the explicit mention of faculty holding Ph.D. degrees (awarded) as on 31 March of each year in faculty files demonstrates a systematic approach to tracking and promoting doctoral qualifications. The institution maintains degree certificates in faculty files to verify these qualifications, ensuring compliance with NAAC standards. The proactive sanctioning of sabbaticals and financial support for doctoral research reflects a strong institutional commitment to increasing the proportion of full-time teachers with Ph.D. degrees, thereby contributing to the overall academic excellence and research output of the institution.

This expansion highlights the institution's success in broadening its scope from student-centric activities to include faculty mobility and professional development. The steady rise from 8 to 15 linkages over four years underscores the institution's effective implementation of policies aimed at strengthening industry-academia partnerships and academic collaborations. These linkages provide students with valuable real-world experience through internships and OJT, while faculty exchange programs contribute to the enrichment of teaching and research capabilities. The inclusion of field trips and research collaborations further supports the holistic development of students and the advancement of academic inquiry. The institution's ability to maintain and grow these linkages despite external challenges demonstrates its resilience and proactive approach to educational enhancement. Overall, the data indicates a robust and evolving ecosystem of external linkages that align with the institution's mission to provide high-quality, industry-relevant education and foster a culture of continuous learning and professional growth.

metrics.title: Adequate infrastructure for teaching-learning
metrics.description: The institution has adequate facilities for teaching-learning: classrooms, laboratories, computing equipment, specialized workshops (CNC, laser cutting), smart rooms, and campus land area.
metrics.narrative_draft:
The institution maintains adequate and advanced infrastructure to support teaching-learning processes, with a strong emphasis on hands-on, student-centric pedagogy. Central to this infrastructure is the advanced Maker Studio, established in 2017, which is equipped with specialized workshops including 3D printers, laser cutters, PCB milling machines, and CNC machines. These facilities enable rapid prototyping and have facilitated the creation of 310 student prototypes, directly supporting project-based learning (PBL) initiatives that begin in the first year of study. Students are encouraged to complete projects that cross multiple subjects, utilizing the resources available in the Maker Studio to bridge theoretical knowledge with practical application.

To further enhance technical education, the college provides an on-campus Component Library, allowing students to borrow electronic sensors, microcontrollers, and actuators for both academic and innovative projects. This resource is integral to hands-on demonstrations in core courses and supports the flipped classroom model adopted by faculty. Additionally, the institution features an E-Learning Studio equipped with a light-board recording setup, which is used to create short concept videos, thereby enriching the digital learning ecosystem. The college also serves as an IIT Bombay remote centre for NMEICT/FOSSEE workshops, indicating a robust connection with premier institutions for continuous faculty development and resource sharing.

Beyond engineering-specific facilities, the institution supports diverse academic disciplines through specialized infrastructure such as the Observatory (UXO), established in 2020, which focuses on remote-sensing and GIS research on urban growth. This facility has contributed to the production of six research papers and two consultancy projects, demonstrating the versatility of the campus infrastructure in supporting both undergraduate teaching and advanced research activities. The combination of specialized workshops, digital learning tools, and subject-specific laboratories ensures that the institution provides a comprehensive environment conducive to modern, interactive, and outcome-oriented education.

metrics.narrative_draft: Pillai College of Engineering, Panvel, maintains adequate infrastructure and active programming to support sports, games, and cultural activities for its student community. The institution provides dedicated physical spaces for athletic and wellness activities, specifically the Ground Floor Conclave and Gymkhana, which serve as primary venues for physical training and student engagement. These facilities are actively utilized to host intensive workshops and physical education initiatives that promote student well-being and safety. A notable example of the utilization of these facilities is the 'Nirbhaya' Five-Day Intensive Self-Defense & Personal Safety Training Workshop, organized by the Women Development Cell (WDC) in collaboration with the Navi Mumbai Police Commissionerate's Nirbhaya Pathak Squad. Conducted from 11th December 2023 to 15th December 2023, this event leveraged the Gymkhana and Conclave spaces to provide practical martial arts maneuvers, situational awareness protocols, and emergency response training. The workshop successfully engaged 320 female students from first, second, and third-year degree programs, demonstrating the institution's capacity to host large-scale physical training events. Beyond physical sports, the institution actively fosters a vibrant cultural environment through the organization of the annual cultural festival, ALEGRIA. This flagship event serves as a platform for students to showcase their artistic and cultural talents, contributing to a holistic educational experience. The institution's commitment to these activities is further evidenced by the active involvement of student councils and the systematic organization of various competitions and events at the institutional level. By integrating physical fitness initiatives with cultural celebrations, Pillai College of Engineering ensures that its facilities are not only available but are effectively utilized to enhance the overall development and engagement of its student body.

metrics.narrative_draft:
The institution maintains a robust and transparent organizational structure that strictly adheres to statutory requirements and regulatory norms. The governance framework is anchored by a well-defined Governing Body, which provides strategic direction and oversight to the institution's academic and administrative functions. This body ensures that the institution operates in alignment with the broader educational policies and statutory mandates applicable to higher education institutions. 

The administrative setup is structured hierarchically under the leadership of the Principal and the Registrar. The Principal serves as the chief executive officer, responsible for the overall academic and administrative management, while the Registrar oversees the administrative and operational aspects, ensuring smooth day-to-day functioning. This dual leadership model ensures a balance between academic excellence and administrative efficiency. 

Regarding human resource management, the institution follows service rules framed by MES (Maharashtra Education Society or relevant statutory body, as implied by context). These rules provide a clear framework for employee conduct, duties, and responsibilities. Furthermore, the institution has established a recruitment and promotion policy that is explicitly aligned with the norms set by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the University Grants Commission (UGC). This alignment ensures that the hiring and career progression of faculty and non-teaching staff are conducted fairly, transparently, and in compliance with national standards. 

To ensure a supportive and accountable work environment, the institution has implemented effective grievance redressal mechanisms. These mechanisms provide structured channels for employees and students to raise concerns, ensuring that issues are addressed promptly and fairly. The existence of these statutory bodies and policies demonstrates the institution's commitment to good governance, legal compliance, and the welfare of its stakeholders. The organizational structure is designed to facilitate efficient decision-making, accountability, and continuous improvement in institutional performance.

metrics.title: Effective welfare measures
metrics.description: The institution has effective welfare measures for teaching and non-teaching staff. Detail training support, sponsorships, leaves (sick, earned, casual), EPF schemes, health programs, and credit societies.
metrics.narrative_draft:
Mahatma Education Society (MES) demonstrates a commitment to the professional development and welfare of its teaching staff through structured policies and financial support mechanisms. A key initiative is the MES Faculty Higher Qualification Upgradation Policy, which facilitates higher academic qualifications for faculty members. This is exemplified by the recent sanction of a six-month paid sabbatical study leave for Prof. Archana Dongre, Associate Professor in the Department of Information Technology, as detailed in Memorandum No. MES/HR/EDU-LEAVE/2023/452 dated 10th August 2023. The Board of Management approved this leave from 1st September 2023 to 28th February 2024 to allow the faculty member to finalize experimental benchmarking and submit her Ph.D. thesis titled 'Optimized Machine Learning Pipelines for Healthcare Telemetry' to the University of Mumbai at Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute (VJTI). 

The welfare measures associated with this leave include comprehensive financial support to alleviate the economic burden on the faculty member. Specifically, a monthly Doctoral Research Fellowship Allowance is sanctioned for the entire duration of the leave. Additionally, the institution provides complete reimbursement for university thesis submission fees and doctoral defense examination fees, contingent upon the submission of official fee receipts. To ensure that academic operations are not disrupted during the faculty member's absence, the institution implements a temporary adjustment of teaching workloads by assigning guest faculty. This approach ensures that the research completion process is supported without compromising the quality of education for students. These measures reflect an effective welfare framework that prioritizes the academic growth of teaching staff while maintaining institutional stability. The involvement of the Secretary of Mahatma Education Society and Dr. Sandeep M. Joshi, Principal, in the sanctioning process underscores the institutional endorsement of these welfare initiatives.

metrics.title: IQAC initiatives
metrics.description: Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) has contributed significantly to institutionalizing quality assurance: Project-Based Learning, Component Library, AAA audits, and Faculty Appraisals.
metrics.narrative_draft:
The Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC), established in 2017, has played a pivotal role in institutionalizing quality assurance mechanisms within the institution. A cornerstone of its operational framework is the conduct of annual Academic and Administrative Audits (AAA), which serve to rigorously review teaching-learning processes and institutional governance structures. Beyond periodic audits, the IQAC has pioneered the implementation of Project-Based Learning (PBL) and established the Component Library, initiatives designed to enhance practical learning outcomes and resource accessibility for students and faculty alike.

To ensure continuous monitoring of academic performance, the IQAC oversees the Academic Monitoring System (AMS). This system dynamically tracks critical academic indicators, including student attendance, daily lecture entries, and syllabus coverage across all academic programs. This data-driven approach allows for real-time intervention and ensures that academic standards are consistently met. Furthermore, the IQAC is responsible for the systematic conduct of Faculty Appraisals, ensuring that teaching staff are evaluated against defined quality benchmarks to foster professional development and accountability.

The scope of IQAC initiatives has expanded significantly over recent years, reflecting a growing commitment to a quality culture. In the 2019-20 academic year, the cell undertook five major initiatives, primarily focusing on Academic and Administrative Audits and Faculty Appraisals. The following year, 2020-21, saw four initiatives, with a shift towards digital quality assurance, including online teaching quality checks and the refinement of the feedback system. metrics.narrative_draft:
Pillai College of Engineering, Panvel, has actively promoted gender equity and safety through structured programs and infrastructure audits, particularly during the 2023-2024 academic year. A key initiative was the organization of the 'Nirbhaya' Five-Day Intensive Self-Defense & Personal Safety Training Workshop, conducted by the Women Development Cell (WDC) in collaboration with the Navi Mumbai Police Commissionerate's Nirbhaya Pathak Squad. Held from December 11 to December 15, 2023, at the Ground Floor Conclave & Gymkhana, this program was designed to empower female engineering students and staff members with practical safety skills. The workshop featured demonstrations by Lady Police Inspector Sunita More and her team, covering martial arts maneuvers, situational awareness protocols for public transport, and the use of emergency cyber-helpline tools, specifically the Police Dial 112 SOS mobile application. A total of 320 female students from first, second, and third-year degree programs successfully completed the five-day physical training, highlighting the institution's commitment to ensuring the physical security and confidence of its female student body.

In addition to direct training programs, the institution has implemented comprehensive gender sensitivity facilities and safety audits to foster an equitable campus environment. The 2023-2024 Gender Sensitivity Facilities & Women Campus Safety Audit Report, submitted by WDC Convener Dr. Mansi Subhedar and countersigned by Principal Dr. Sandeep M. Joshi, details the deployment of high-definition CCTV cameras at all academic block entrances, corridors, parking zones, and library areas, monitored centrally from the security control room. The audit confirms the installation of sanitary napkin vending machines and automated incinerators in women's restrooms across Academic Blocks 1, 2, and 3. Furthermore, the institution provides spacious, well-furnished Girls' Common Rooms equipped with first-aid kits. To address grievances and promote awareness, the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) and WDC conduct regular sessions against sexual harassment, with emergency SOS contact numbers and helpline details visibly displayed on campus boards. These combined efforts in training, infrastructure, and policy enforcement demonstrate a robust framework for gender equity promotion at the institution.

The institution has implemented comprehensive safety and security measures, including the deployment of high-definition CCTV cameras at all academic block entrances, corridor intersections, parking zones, and library corridors. These surveillance systems are monitored centrally from the security control room to ensure 24x7 safety. To address hygiene and comfort, the college has installed fully functional sanitary napkin vending machines and automated incinerators in women's restrooms across Academic Blocks 1, 2, and 3. The functional status of these vending machines is regularly inspected by the Women Development Cell (WDC) to ensure uninterrupted service. Additionally, spacious, clean, and well-furnished Girls' Common Rooms are provided, equipped with first-aid medical kits and resting facilities to promote student well-being. In terms of grievance redressal and support, the institution maintains an active Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) and a Women Development Cell (WDC). These bodies conduct regular awareness sessions against sexual harassment and ensure that emergency SOS contact numbers and Police Dial 112 helpline details are visibly displayed on campus boards. The WDC, led by Convener Dr. Mansi Subhedar and countersigned by Principal Dr. Sandeep M. Joshi, actively engages with the student body. For instance, 320 female students across first, second, and third years successfully completed a five-day physical training program, which included the use of the Police Dial 112 app. The institution further supports gender-sensitive initiatives through student-led bodies, such as the Canteen Committee, which conducts hygiene audits, and the Anti-Ragging Committee, which organizes awareness sessions. These collective efforts reflect the institution's dedication to fostering a gender-sensitive campus culture through infrastructure, security, and active student engagement.
